meta.name: Cloudflare Application Security Specialist
meta.notes: Initial release covering Cloudflare application security topics: proxy fundamentals, TLS modes, WAF, DDoS protection, bot management, rate limiting, API Shield, Page Shield, Cloudflare Access, and security observability. | 2026-05-23 keyword-balance pass | 2026-06-01 +6 questions to unlock learning path | [scheduled-agent hardening pass 2026-06-07: stripped self-defeating "but does not..." clauses from 10 distractors that leaked the correct answer, rewrote wrong options as confident plausible misconceptions, rebalanced positions to A/B/C/D = 4/4/4/4 with no triple-runs, trimmed length tells where the correct answer was the longest option, moved per-distractor why-wrong reasoning into explanations only]

questions.question: A team adds a new origin server `api.example.com` in Cloudflare DNS but observes that Cloudflare WAF rules never fire for requests to that hostname. What is the most likely cause?
options: The record is set to `DNS only` (gray-cloud), so traffic bypasses Cloudflare's reverse proxy and the WAF, DDoS, and caching layers along with it
Universal SSL is still pending issuance for the hostname, and WAF Managed Rules are gated on a valid TLS certificate being active for the zone first
On the Free plan, WAF Managed Rules apply only to apex records and are not evaluated for proxied subdomains in the same zone
An Origin Rules entry is intercepting traffic for the new subdomain before the WAF engine has a chance to evaluate the request
questions.explanation: For Cloudflare to act as a reverse proxy and apply security features (WAF, DDoS protection, bot management, caching), the DNS record must be proxied (orange-cloud). A `DNS only` (gray-cloud) record resolves directly to the origin IP and bypasses Cloudflare entirely. SSL issuance does not pause WAF — Managed Rules run regardless of certificate state. WAF Managed Rules apply to all proxied hostnames in the zone, not just the apex. Origin Rules adjust how Cloudflare reaches the origin (Host header, port, SNI); they run after the WAF and cannot disable it.

questions.question: An operator wants end-to-end encryption between visitor and Cloudflare and between Cloudflare and origin, and wants Cloudflare to verify that the origin certificate is valid and trusted before forwarding traffic. Which SSL/TLS encryption mode meets all of these requirements?
options: Flexible, which encrypts visitor-to-Cloudflare traffic and reaches the origin over plain HTTP for compatibility with legacy origins
Full, which encrypts both connection legs and accepts any origin certificate Cloudflare can negotiate, including self-signed ones
Full (strict), which encrypts both legs and requires the origin certificate to be signed by a trusted CA or Cloudflare's Origin CA
Off, which disables Cloudflare's TLS termination and serves the zone over HTTP without encrypting either leg
questions.explanation: Full (strict) encrypts both visitor-to-Cloudflare and Cloudflare-to-origin and validates the origin certificate against a trusted CA (or Cloudflare's Origin CA). Full encrypts both legs but accepts self-signed or expired origin certificates with no validation. Flexible only encrypts the visitor-to-Cloudflare leg and forwards plaintext to the origin. Off disables HTTPS at Cloudflare entirely and provides no encryption.

questions.question: A team wants broad coverage against SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and other common web attacks without hand-writing one rule per attack pattern. Which Cloudflare WAF capability is the most direct way to achieve this?
options: Author a Custom Rule with a regex that matches SQL keywords such as `SELECT` or `UNION` in the query string of every incoming request
Enable Rate Limiting at one request per minute on any request whose path contains `/login`, since SQLi probes typically arrive as repeated submissions over time
Turn on Page Shield in monitor mode so any third-party script containing SQL or HTML markers is flagged on the dashboard for review
Enable the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset (and OWASP Core Ruleset), which provides curated, updated detections for SQLi, XSS, and other common attack classes
questions.explanation: Cloudflare Managed Rulesets (the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset and the OWASP Core Ruleset) are curated and continually updated detections for SQLi, XSS, RCE, and other common attack classes — the standard way to get broad WAF coverage out of the box. A single hand-written keyword regex is brittle and produces many false positives or misses encoded payloads. Rate Limiting throttles request volume but does not inspect for injection content. Page Shield monitors client-side JavaScript loaded in the browser; it does not block server-side injection attempts.

questions.question: A site is hit by a high-volume HTTP GET flood from many residential IPs whose requests complete a valid TCP and TLS handshake but then exhaust origin worker capacity at the application layer. Which Cloudflare protection layer is purpose-built to mitigate this attack?
options: The HTTP DDoS Attack Protection ruleset, which inspects layer-7 request patterns at the edge and challenges or blocks suspected attack traffic before it reaches the origin
The L3/4 DDoS Protection ruleset, which inspects packet headers at the network layer and blocks volumetric floods such as SYN, UDP amplification, and reflection attacks
Argo Smart Routing, which selects lower-latency paths between Cloudflare data centers and the origin so legitimate users feel less impact under regional congestion
Cache Reserve, which persists cached objects in R2 so that repeated requests for the same URL are served from cache and remove load from the origin
questions.explanation: An HTTP GET flood that completes TLS is a layer-7 attack. Cloudflare's HTTP DDoS Attack Protection ruleset analyzes layer-7 request patterns (per-zone fingerprints, anomaly rates) and challenges or blocks attack traffic at the edge. L3/4 DDoS Protection handles network-layer floods (SYN, UDP amplification, reflection) but does not parse HTTP request semantics. Argo Smart Routing is a performance feature for path selection and does not classify attack traffic. Cache Reserve improves cache hit ratio but cannot identify or block malicious requests.

questions.question: A web application must allow verified search engine crawlers and other known-good bots through unchanged while challenging or blocking unverified automated traffic. Which Cloudflare feature directly supports this distinction?
options: WAF Sensitive Data Detection, which scans response bodies for PII and challenges any automated client that retrieves content protected by the ruleset
Workers placed in front of the application, which inspect User-Agent strings against a curated list and reject requests from any known bad bot signature
Tiered Cache, which routes bot traffic to dedicated edge nodes so that automated requests do not compete with human visitors for cache capacity at the origin
Bot Management (with Super Bot Fight Mode on lower plans), which assigns a per-request bot score and recognizes verified bots that can be allowed independently
questions.explanation: Bot Management (Enterprise) and Super Bot Fight Mode (Pro/Biz) assign a per-request bot score and recognize a maintained list of verified bots (Googlebot, Bingbot, and others) that can be allowed while suspected automated traffic is challenged or blocked. WAF Sensitive Data Detection inspects response bodies for data leaks, not request automation. User-Agent strings are trivially spoofed by attackers, so a Workers UA filter is unreliable. Tiered Cache is a cache topology and has no bot classification.

questions.question: An administrator must cap each visitor to ten POST requests per minute against `/api/login` and block offenders for ten minutes when the cap is exceeded. Which Cloudflare feature is purpose-built for this requirement?
options: WAF Managed Rules in the OWASP Core Ruleset, whose brute-force category fires after a fixed attempt threshold per source IP across the zone
A Cloudflare Workers script that maintains an in-memory counter per request path, since Workers retain state across invocations within an edge data center
Advanced Rate Limiting rules, which let an administrator define a request count, period, characteristics (such as IP), action, and a mitigation timeout window
Page Rules with a `Block` action attached, which short-circuit any matching URL once traffic volume for that path rises above a configured threshold
questions.explanation: Advanced Rate Limiting rules let you specify a counting expression, request threshold, period, characteristics (such as IP, header, cookie), action (block, challenge, log), and a mitigation duration — directly matching the requirement. OWASP rules detect attack payloads (SQLi, XSS, traversal) and do not implement a generic per-IP request-rate counter. Plain Workers have no durable per-invocation memory across the global edge — durable state requires Durable Objects or KV. Page Rules adjust caching and forwarding; they do not perform request counting.

questions.question: An API serves only mobile clients that ship with X.509 client certificates issued by an internal CA. The team wants Cloudflare to reject any request that does not present a valid certificate from that CA before the request reaches origin. Which API Shield feature implements this?
options: Mutual TLS (mTLS) enforcement, which validates that the client presents a certificate signed by an uploaded mTLS root CA before the request is forwarded to the origin
API Discovery, which observes traffic over time and auto-generates an OpenAPI document of the endpoints actually being called by clients in production
Schema Validation, which compares incoming request bodies to a stored OpenAPI schema and blocks requests whose fields, types, or values diverge from the contract
JWT Validation, which decodes and verifies bearer tokens in the `Authorization` header and rejects requests whose JWTs fail signature or expiration checks at the edge
questions.explanation: API Shield's Mutual TLS (mTLS) feature requires that clients present a certificate signed by a CA uploaded into the zone, and Cloudflare validates it at the edge before forwarding. API Discovery inventories endpoints from observed traffic — it does not authenticate the client. Schema Validation enforces request structure but accepts any client regardless of identity. JWT Validation checks bearer tokens, which any client that obtains the token can replay; only mTLS proves possession of a private key bound to a specific certificate.

questions.question: An e-commerce site is concerned about Magecart-style attacks in which an attacker injects malicious code into a third-party JavaScript dependency to skim payment data from the checkout page. Which Cloudflare feature is purpose-built to detect this class of client-side supply-chain attack?
options: Workers KV, which stores small key-value entries at the edge and can sign script payloads so that browsers verify their integrity at load time
Page Shield, which uses browser telemetry to inventory the JavaScript that visitors actually execute and alerts on new, modified, or suspicious scripts
WAF Sensitive Data Detection, which scans outgoing HTML response bodies for payment card numbers and removes any scripts that handle that data downstream
Cloudflare Tunnel, which creates an outbound-only encrypted link from the origin to Cloudflare so that scripts cannot be modified in transit between origin and edge
questions.explanation: Page Shield is Cloudflare's client-side security product. It uses Content Security Policy reports and browser telemetry to inventory the JavaScript that visitors actually load and to alert when scripts change, are added, or are flagged as malicious — directly addressing Magecart-style attacks on third-party dependencies. Workers KV is a key-value store and has no script-integrity feature. WAF Sensitive Data Detection scans for response-side PII leaks; it does not track script provenance. Cloudflare Tunnel secures the origin connection, not browser-side script execution.

questions.question: A team must protect an internal admin panel hosted behind Cloudflare so that only employees from a specific email domain who pass MFA can reach it, and the panel must not be publicly accessible. Which Cloudflare capability provides this identity-aware access?
options: WAF Custom Rules that inspect the Cf-Connecting-IP header against a hardcoded office IP allowlist and additionally require an `X-Employee` header on every request
Geo-Block WAF rules combined with a Page Rule that restricts the admin path to the company's country and disables HTTP/2 for that hostname's traffic
The Cloudflare Tunnel daemon installed on each employee's laptop, which mints an mTLS certificate at login and uses it to authenticate every outbound connection
Cloudflare Access (Zero Trust), which authenticates visitors through an identity provider and enforces per-app policies such as email domain, MFA, and device posture
questions.explanation: Cloudflare Access is the Zero Trust product that gates an application behind an identity provider (Okta, Google, Entra ID, and others) and enforces per-app policies such as email domain, MFA, group membership, and device posture. IP allowlists and custom headers do not authenticate user identity and break for off-network employees. Geo-blocking restricts by country, not user, and disabling HTTP/2 is irrelevant to access control. Cloudflare Tunnel runs on origins to expose private servers; it is not an end-user identity client.

questions.question: After a suspected scraping incident, an engineer needs to inspect per-request security decisions for the past several hours — including which WAF, bot, or rate-limit rule fired and what action was applied. In the Cloudflare dashboard, where should they look first?
options: The Cloudflare Analytics overview tab, which shows zone-level visitor and bandwidth graphs and breaks down per-rule actions per hour in the security panel
The Workers Analytics tab, which records script invocation counts and CPU time and lists requests that bypassed Workers due to a security action upstream
The DNS Analytics dashboard, which records every authoritative DNS query the zone served and includes any HTTP-level firewall decisions reached for the domain
The Security Events view under the zone's Security section, which records per-request WAF, bot, rate-limit, and Custom Rule actions filterable by rule and time
questions.explanation: Security Events (formerly Firewall Events) is the per-request security log in the Cloudflare dashboard, showing which security service (WAF, Bot Management, Rate Limiting, DDoS, Custom Rules) acted on a request and what action was taken. The Analytics overview presents aggregated trends, not per-request rows. Workers Analytics covers script execution metrics for Workers code only. DNS Analytics tracks DNS queries to the authoritative servers and has no HTTP-layer firewall data.

questions.question: A team needs to expose a web application running on a private server that has no public IP and sits behind a firewall that blocks all inbound connections. They want Cloudflare to reach it securely without opening any inbound port. Which Cloudflare product is purpose-built for this?
options: A proxied (orange-cloud) DNS A record pointing at the server's public IP, with a firewall exception allowing inbound 443 from Cloudflare's published IP ranges
Cloudflare Tunnel, which runs the `cloudflared` connector on the origin to make an outbound-only encrypted link to Cloudflare, with no inbound ports needed
A Page Rule that rewrites the request to the server's internal hostname, so Cloudflare resolves the private address directly without any agent installed on the origin
Spectrum, which proxies arbitrary TCP and UDP ports and exposes a private server by mapping its internal IP to a public Cloudflare anycast address automatically
questions.explanation: Cloudflare Tunnel runs the `cloudflared` connector on the origin, which dials out to Cloudflare over an encrypted connection; because the link is outbound-only, the firewall can keep all inbound ports closed and the server needs no public IP. A proxied A record still requires a publicly reachable origin IP and inbound 443 from Cloudflare's ranges. Page Rules adjust request handling but cannot route to an unreachable private host. Spectrum proxies TCP/UDP applications but still requires the origin to be reachable from Cloudflare.

questions.question: A site owner wants requests for static assets (images, CSS, JS) to be served from Cloudflare's edge cache to reduce origin load, while ensuring HTML pages are always fetched fresh from the origin. Which Cloudflare behavior or setting should they rely on?
options: Cloudflare caches a default set of static file extensions and does not cache HTML by default, and Cache Rules can refine this per-path behavior
Cloudflare caches every response including HTML by default, so the owner adds a Cache Rule that explicitly bypasses cache for static asset extensions
Cloudflare caches nothing until the origin sends a `Cf-Cache: store` response header, which the owner configures on the routes serving static assets
Caching is controlled by the WAF, so the owner enables a Managed Ruleset that caches assets matching common image and script signatures at the edge
questions.explanation: Cloudflare's default cache behavior caches a set of static file types (by extension) and does not cache HTML unless explicitly told to — which already matches the requirement. Cache Rules (the successor to cache-related Page Rules) let you refine caching per path, extension, or other criteria. The reversed-default option is backwards: Cloudflare does not cache HTML by default. There is no `Cf-Cache: store` request gate. The WAF inspects and blocks requests; it is not the caching engine.

questions.question: A security engineer wants to block all traffic to the zone originating from a specific country except for a small set of trusted office IP addresses, which must always be allowed regardless of country. Which Cloudflare configuration expresses this most directly?
options: Enable the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset, whose geo-reputation rule blocks the country while exempting any IP marked as a corporate address in IP Intelligence
Set the zone's Security Level to 'I'm Under Attack', which challenges every visitor from the targeted country while allowing known office IPs through transparently
Create a WAF Custom Rule that blocks traffic when `ip.geoip.country` matches the target country AND the source IP is not in the trusted office IP allowlist
Add the country to the zone's IP Access Rules block list, and Cloudflare automatically skips any source IP whose ASN belongs to a business broadband provider
questions.explanation: WAF Custom Rules use an expression language where you can combine conditions — for example block when `ip.geoip.country eq "XX"` AND the client IP is not in your trusted set (or place an allow/skip rule for the office IPs ahead of the block rule). This precisely encodes 'block this country except these IPs'. The Managed Ruleset targets known attack classes, not arbitrary geo policy with an IP exception. 'I'm Under Attack' mode challenges nearly all visitors site-wide and is not a per-country, per-IP allow/block tool. IP Access Rules can block a country but do not auto-skip based on a guessed business ASN.

questions.question: An operator wants to issue a free TLS certificate that is trusted specifically by Cloudflare for the Cloudflare-to-origin leg in Full (strict) mode, without buying a publicly trusted certificate for the origin. Which Cloudflare offering provides this?
options: Universal SSL, which Cloudflare provisions automatically to secure the visitor-to-Cloudflare leg and can also be installed on the origin to satisfy Full (strict) validation
Cloudflare Origin CA certificates, which Cloudflare issues for free and are trusted by Cloudflare's edge for the Cloudflare-to-origin connection in Full (strict) mode
Keyless SSL, which lets the origin present any self-signed certificate because the private key stays on the customer side and Cloudflare skips origin validation
Authenticated Origin Pulls, which generates a public DigiCert-signed certificate for the origin so that browsers and Cloudflare both trust the origin directly
questions.explanation: Cloudflare Origin CA issues free TLS certificates signed by Cloudflare's own origin CA; installed on the origin, they are trusted by Cloudflare's edge and satisfy Full (strict) for the Cloudflare-to-origin leg without a paid public certificate. Universal SSL is the front-end certificate served to visitors and is not installed on the origin. Keyless SSL keeps the visitor-facing private key on the customer's side; it does not waive origin certificate validation. Authenticated Origin Pulls is the reverse direction — the origin verifies that requests come from Cloudflare via a client certificate, not a server certificate the origin presents.

questions.question: A serverless team wants to run custom request-handling logic — such as adding security headers and routing — at Cloudflare's edge close to users, without provisioning or managing any servers. Which Cloudflare product runs this code at the edge?
options: Cloudflare Pages Functions, which run code only as part of a statically deployed Pages site and cannot operate in front of an existing proxied origin
Cloudflare Workers, which run developer-supplied JavaScript or WebAssembly on Cloudflare's edge network in response to requests, with no servers to manage
Cloudflare Load Balancing, which runs custom request-handling scripts on each pool member to add headers and route traffic before forwarding to the selected origin
Cloudflare Stream, which executes edge logic to transform and route incoming requests while primarily serving as the platform's adaptive video delivery service
questions.explanation: Cloudflare Workers is the serverless edge compute platform: you deploy JavaScript or WebAssembly that runs on Cloudflare's global network in response to requests, letting you add headers, rewrite, route, or generate responses with no servers to manage. Pages Functions are Workers-based but tied to a Pages project and not the general answer for arbitrary proxied origins. Load Balancing distributes traffic across pools by health and steering rules and does not run user code. Stream is a video encoding and delivery service, not a general edge-compute runtime.

questions.question: A team running an API behind API Shield has uploaded an OpenAPI specification and wants Cloudflare to reject any request whose body or parameters do not conform to the documented contract (wrong types, missing required fields, disallowed values). Which API Shield feature enforces this?
options: API Discovery, which observes live traffic to learn endpoints and then automatically blocks any request to an endpoint that was not seen during the learning period
Mutual TLS (mTLS), which validates that each client presents a certificate from an uploaded CA and rejects malformed bodies that fail the certificate handshake
Schema Validation, which compares incoming requests against the uploaded OpenAPI schema and applies the configured action to requests that violate the contract
Sequence Mitigation, which enforces the documented field types by requiring API calls to arrive in the exact order defined in the uploaded OpenAPI specification
questions.explanation: API Shield Schema Validation enforces the uploaded OpenAPI schema, checking requests against the contract (required fields, types, allowed values, paths and methods) and applying the configured action — log or block — to non-conforming requests. API Discovery inventories endpoints from observed traffic; it does not validate request structure against a schema. mTLS authenticates client identity and has nothing to do with request body conformance. Sequence-based controls relate to the order of API calls (abuse detection of unusual call sequences), not field-level schema enforcement.
